title: Fast-path cache key drops `version` while the canonical key keeps it, so run-sourced catboost/rustystats models load from disk twice and leave a permanently-orphaned duplicate cache entry (and skewed hit/miss counters); pyfunc loses the fast path entirely
description: load_mlflow_model has two cache-key construction sites that disagree for `source_type="run"` whenever a non-empty `version` is supplied. The fast-path (lines 893-900) hardcodes `version=""`, so `_model_cache_key` (lines 311-313: truthy version -> 5-tuple, else 4-tuple) returns the 4-tuple `("run", run_id, artifact_path, task)`. The slow-path (lines 968-974) passes `version=resolved_version`, and for a run source `resolve_mlflow_source` returns `resolved_version = version` unchanged (_mlflow_utils.py:101,109-111). Production callers ALWAYS pass `version=config.get("version", "latest")` even for run sources (src/haute/_builders.py:1196; src/haute/_model_explainability.py:569; threaded through ModelScorer._load_scoring_model_uncached at _model_scorer.py:1063-1070). With `version="latest"` (truthy) the slow-path stores the model under the 5-tuple `("run", run_id, "latest", artifact_path, task)` while the fast-path only ever looks up / stores the 4-tuple. The two keys can never coincide. CONSEQUENCES for catboost/rustystats (the only in-repo producers): call 1 (cold) misses the 4-tuple, finds no disk file, falls to the slow path, downloads + loads + put(5-tuple); call 2 misses the 4-tuple again (model is under the 5-tuple), now finds the disk file present and re-loads it from disk via the disk-cache fast path, put(4-tuple) — so the model is deserialized from disk TWICE before steady state, TWO cache MISSES are recorded for one logical model (skewing get_model_cache_stats hit-rate), and the 5-tuple entry becomes dead weight that the steady-state fast path never hits again, permanently consuming one of only _MODEL_CACHE_MAX_SIZE=16 slots until LRU-evicted (effectively halving cache capacity for run-sourced models). For pyfunc run-sourced models the disk-cache fast-path block is skipped entirely (it is gated on `flavor in ("catboost","rustystats")` at line 910), so the 4-tuple lookup at line 901 ALWAYS misses and EVERY call falls through to resolve_mlflow_source() — defeating the very tracking-server round-trip the fast path exists to avoid (per the comment at lines 888-892). No price-correctness impact (same model bytes, same run_id+artifact_path), but it is a real cache-coherence defect: redundant disk loads, a permanently duplicated/orphaned cache entry, defeated fast-path, and inaccurate observability counters.
evidence: load_mlflow_model fast-path: line 894-900 `fast_key = _model_cache_key(source_type=source_type, run_id=run_id, version="", artifact_path=artifact_path, task=task)` -> with version="" the helper (line 311-313: `if version: return (source_type, run_id, version, artifact_path, task)` else 4-tuple) yields `("run", run_id, artifact_path, task)`. Slow-path: line 968-974 `cache_key = _model_cache_key(... version=resolved_version ...)`; resolve_mlflow_source returns resolved_version=version for run source (_mlflow_utils.py:100-101 `resolved_version = version`, and the `elif source_type == "run"` branch at 109-111 never reassigns it). Caller default: _builders.py:1196 `version=config.get("version", "latest")` (passed to ModelScorer.version -> _load_scoring_model_uncached -> load_mlflow_model). For a run source with version="latest": fast_key=4-tuple, cache_key=5-tuple -> disjoint. Disk-cache fast-path put(fast_key) at line 936 vs slow-path put(cache_key) at line 1028 store under different keys; the gate at line 910 (`if flavor in ("catboost", "rustystats")`) is why pyfunc never reaches the disk-cache fast path and thus always falls through to the network resolve. Not in the two known findings (which concern training-vs-scored prediction semantics and the pyfunc loader_module missing _load_pyfunc symbol) and not in the catalog (which covers output-schema/deploy version staleness, not this intra-function fast/slow key split).
